newsitem.title: USA: J.P. Morgan fund deal seen good match.
newsitem.headline: J.P. Morgan fund deal seen good match.

text.p: J.P. Morgan & Co Inc, which announced plans Wednesday to buy a 45 percent stake in U.S. mutual fund company American Century Cos, has found a partner with complementary rather than overlapping strengths, industry analysts said.

"It's interesting to see that Morgan, which has catered to a highly affluent and essentially almost an institutional marketplace is now recognizing the tremendous profitability of the retail side of the business," said Burton Greenwald, a Philadelphia-based mutual fund consultant.

He said the combination of the "Morgan cachet" and its expertise particularly in the international arena, when teamed with the strong domestic business of American Century, will create an "even more powerful factor in the business."
J.P. Morgan will pay about $900 million cash for the 45 percent stake.

In a telephone interview, American Century president William Lyons said J.P. Morgan has an option to raise its stake to 50 percent. But he said Morgan is not seeking to acquire control and in fact the founding Stowers family would still have control if its stake were 50 percent.
"Morgan's desire is to keep American Century independent," Lyons said, adding that J.P. Morgan was looking for a partner to help it service large institutional clients.

Lyons said that J.P. Morgan, a New York financial service powerhouse with roots going back to 1838, and Kansas City, Mo.-based American Century have similar cultures. He said both firms put customers first and take a "team-oriented" approach to running the business rather than relying on star managers.
Lyons said American Century's strengths are its record-keeping know-how and expertise in the aggressive growth equities area.
J.P. Morgan said a new partnership to be formed by itself and American Century will initially focus on offering defined contribution pension plans such as 401(K) plans to corporate plan sponsors.

Lyons said it would be a full service, bundled product. He also said that over time, the partnership will provide American Century with distribution outside of the U.S. but that was not the near-term focus.
A Wall Street analyst, who decined to be identified, said the deal was positive for J.P. Morgan because it expanded its presence in an area that has higher margins.

However the Moody's Investors Service said it was reviewing J.P. Morgan's long term debt ratings for a possible downgrade. Moody's said the American Century deal adds about $750 million of goodwill to the balance sheet.

Standard & Poor's said it affirmed debt J.P. Morgan ratings but the outlook remained negative. S&P said the American Century deal was a "sound strategic move" but a costly one that increases leverage. S&P also said J.P. Morgan remains "one of the premier global banks."

In an unrelated development, American Century Wednesday said holders of former Benham and 20th Century funds voted to change management agreements in the funds. A spokesman, Gunnar Hughes, said that while fees for some of the former Benham funds went up and others went down or were unchanged, the main purpose was to update outdated descriptions of the funds and restrictions.
American Century, then known as 20th Century, acquired the Benham funds in 1995.
